Chief_Complaint.content: Patient presents with itchy, red, sore skin/rash.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Rash onset 4 days ago.
Rash located on chest, hands, and inside elbows.
Patient has prior eczema mainly on arms.
Symptoms include severe pruritus.
Symptoms include soreness of the skin.
Symptoms include dry and cracked skin.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Sx: severe pruritus; soreness; dry/cracked skin

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Rash is causing poor sleep.
Rash is causing difficulty focusing at work.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Impact: poor sleep; difficulty focusing at work

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Rash is painful and interferes with hiking.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Impact: poor sleep; difficulty focusing at work; painful interfering w/ hiking

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient denies pus or blood from the rash.
Patient notes some cracked skin.
Patient denies facial involvement of the rash.
Patient denies change in shower gel or clothing as triggers.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Triggers: denies change in shower gel/clothing

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient is unsure of the trigger for the rash.
Patient denies fever.
Patient denies cough or shortness of breath.
Patient reports bowels are okay.
Patient thinks urination is normal.
Patient previously used eczema creams which helped in the past but not for this episode.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Tx tried: prior eczema creams (helped previously, not now)

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient tried over-the-counter steroid cream without benefit.
Patient recently tried antihistamines without benefit.

Past_Medical_History.content: History of asthma in the past, reported as not anymore.

Medications.content: Patient is not currently taking any medications.

Social_and_Family_History.content: Patient works at a pharmaceutical company as a project manager.
Patient drinks a few beers per week.

Assessment.content: Eczema flare involves chest, hands, and antecubital areas.
Eczema flare associated with dry and cracked skin.
No fever associated with the eczema flare.
No discharge associated with the eczema flare.

Plan_of_Care.content: Prescribe stronger topical steroid for eczema flare.
Use emollients and moisturizers, including in bath or shower, with regular use for 7–10 days before judging response.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Emollients/moisturizers; use in bath/shower; regular use x 7–10 days before judging response

Plan_of_Care.content: Use antihistamines for itch; consider over-the-counter loratadine or chlorphenamine.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Antihistamines for itch: consider OTC loratadine/chlorphenamine

Plan_of_Care.content: Prescription for stronger antihistamine fexofenadine was offered.
Keep a trigger diary including clothing and shower gels/soaps.
Discuss if a suspected trigger is contributing to the rash.

Follow_up_Information.content: Follow up next week if not improving.
Follow_up_Information.source_text: F/u next week if not improving

Physical_Findings.content: Clinician notes that the rash appears familiar and is mainly on chest and back.
Physical_Findings.source_text: Clinician states: “having looked at your skin…rash does appear quite familiar”; mainly chest/back

Review_of_Systems.content: Patient denies cough or shortness of breath.
